pilot.name: Diamond Valley, Eureka County, Nevada
pilot.tagline: Irrigated alfalfa under centre pivots, on falling groundwater

sources.title: Pilot field boundaries (detected from Landsat)
sources.resolution: 30 m (Landsat); each field is the largest circle inside its irrigated footprint
sources.credit: Derived by this project from Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 (USGS/NASA) and the USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer.
sources.message: 14 pilot fields, 37-58 ha, median radius 403 m
sources.notes: OpenET's /geodatabase/metadata/ids endpoint returned HTTP 400 'Invalid geometry' for every request, including the example in its own documentation, so OpenET's field boundaries could not be used. Boundaries here are satellite-derived approximations.

sources.title: GPM IMERG Final Run daily precipitation (GPM_3IMERGDF v07)
sources.resolution: 0.1 degree (~9 x 11 km here); daily accumulation from half-hourly estimates
sources.credit: Huffman, G. J. et al. (2023). GPM IMERG Final Precipitation L3 1 day 0.1 degree x 0.1 degree V07. NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC).
sources.message: 9,039 days; 0 daily files failed; sanity passed
sources.notes: A satellite estimate calibrated to monthly gauge totals, not a rain gauge: it can miss or misplace small summer thunderstorms and struggles with snowfall over mountains. One cell covers many fields. The product's randomError field was not used: its scale in the daily files could not be interpreted reliably.

sources.title: gridMET daily temperature and precipitation (4 km)
sources.credit: Abatzoglou, J. T. (2013). Development of gridded surface meteorological data for ecological applications and modelling. Int. J. Climatol. 33: 121-131. Public domain (CC0).
sources.message: 7 cells; NASA POWER nights are 4.8 degC too warm for the valley floor: frost-free season 134 days raw -> 81 corrected (gridMET itself: 84); annual rain 262 mm -> 229 mm; sanity passed
sources.notes: Used only to bias-correct NASA POWER (monthly delta method). Still a 4 km grid: the coldest hollows frost earlier and later than it shows.

sources.title: Landsat 8/9 surface reflectance (NDVI, bare-soil index)
sources.resolution: 30 m; about every 8 days from two satellites, more where two orbit paths overlap
sources.credit: Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 Science Products courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey and NASA. Accessed through Microsoft Planetary Computer.
sources.message: 461 overpasses, 4,178 field observations, median 299 per field; sanity passed
sources.notes: Pixels flagged cloud, cloud shadow, cirrus or water by the Landsat QA band are dropped; an observation is kept only if at least 60 % of the field is clear. Snow-covered observations are kept but flagged, and excluded from greenness statistics. NDVI shows green cover, not soil health, and saturates in dense alfalfa.

sources.title: MODIS/Terra NDVI 250 m (MOD13Q1 v061)
sources.credit: Didan, K. (2021). MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC. Subsets from ORNL DAAC (2018), MODIS and VIIRS Land Products Global Subsetting and Visualization Tool.
sources.message: 8,050 field-composites, 575 dates; 0 request(s) missing; sanity passed
sources.notes: A 50 ha pivot holds only ~9 MODIS pixels and its edge pixels mix in desert, so MODIS NDVI reads lower than Landsat. The pixel-reliability band was not fetched (it would double the requests to a slow service); the app therefore uses only each year's peak-season maximum, which is robust to cloud and snow.

sources.title: NASA POWER daily agroclimatology
sources.resolution: 0.5 x 0.625 degree (MERRA-2 meteorology), 1 x 1 degree (CERES solar); daily
sources.credit: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project, funded through the NASA Earth Science/Applied Science Program. Public domain.
sources.message: 12,784 daily rows for 1 cell(s); sanity passed
sources.notes: Gridded reanalysis, not an on-farm weather station. Temperatures are later adjusted from the grid-cell mean elevation to each field's elevation with a standard 6.5 degC/km lapse rate (documented in engine/agromet.py).

sources.title: OpenET ensemble evapotranspiration (field scale)
sources.resolution: 30 m (Landsat thermal driven), aggregated to the field polygon; monthly
sources.credit: OpenET (Melton et al. 2022, JAWRA). Ensemble of ALEXI/DisALEXI, eeMETRIC, geeSEBAL, PT-JPL, SIMS and SSEBop, built on Landsat and gridMET. CC BY 4.0.
sources.message: 1,680 field-months for 14 fields; May-Sep model spread (max - min) is a median 35 % of ET; 34 repeated-value months flagged; sanity passed
sources.notes: A model estimate of water actually evaporated and transpired, not a flow-meter reading. The newest six months can still be revised. Winter values are the least reliable (snow, few clear images) and some are repeated across months; those are flagged and left out of seasonal statistics. The field-boundary and field-ID endpoints (/geodatabase/...) returned HTTP 400 for every request, so polygons detected by this project are sent to the raster endpoint instead.

sources.title: Map overlays (PNG)
sources.credit: Derived by this project from Landsat, the crop or land-cover map and SRTM.

sources.title: SMAP enhanced L3 soil moisture (SPL3SMP_E, 9 km)
sources.resolution: 9 km EASE-Grid 2.0 (interpolated from ~33 km radiometer footprints); a retrieval every 2-3 days
sources.credit: O'Neill, P. E. et al. SMAP Enhanced L3 Radiometer Global and Polar Grid Daily 9 km EASE-Grid Soil Moisture. NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center DAAC, Boulder, Colorado.
sources.message: 2,857 retrieval days, 747 cell-months; 0 daily files failed; sanity passed
sources.notes: Top ~5 cm of soil only, and each 9 km cell is mostly desert shrubland with the irrigated pivots mixed in: it shows whether the valley is wetter or drier than usual, not the moisture under one pivot. Anomaly z = (month mean - that calendar month's 2015-2025 mean) / standard deviation; months with under 5 retrieval days are left blank.

sources.title: SRTM 1 arc-second elevation (SRTMGL1 v003)
sources.credit: NASA JPL (2013). NASA Shuttle Radar Topography Mission Global 1 arc second. NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC.
sources.message: elevation 1795-1815 m, field tilt 0.1-0.8 % (plane fit; raw-pixel slope reads 3.1 % because of radar noise); sanity passed
sources.notes: Radar elevation has a few metres of vertical noise: taken pixel by pixel it reads as 2-4 % slope on flat ground. The app uses each field's overall tilt (plane fit), which averages that noise out. The survey predates any land levelling done since 2000.

sources.title: USDA NRCS SSURGO soils (Soil Data Access)
sources.resolution: Vector map units, nominal survey scale 1:24,000 (Order 2-3)
sources.credit: Soil Survey Staff, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO) Database. Public domain.
sources.message: 30 map units; soil table for 14/14 fields; sanity passed
sources.notes: Map units are polygons with representative values, not measurements of every square metre. Values are component-percent weighted (0-30 cm, thickness weighted) and then area weighted over the field.

sources.title: USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer (CDL)
sources.resolution: Source 30 m (10 m for 2024, 2025); clipped with nearest-neighbour sampling to a 30 m Web-Mercator grid; annual
sources.credit: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service Cropland Data Layer. Published crop-specific data layer, USDA-NASS, Washington, DC. Public domain.
sources.notes: A satellite-derived classification, not a ground record: individual field-years can be mislabelled (alfalfa vs other hay is a common confusion). The app shows the share of the field that carried the label and asks the farmer to correct it.

sources.title: USGS groundwater levels (depth to water)
sources.resolution: Point measurements at wells; typically one or two visits a year
sources.credit: U.S. Geological Survey, National Water Information System (USGS Water Data for the Nation). Public domain.
sources.message: 310 wells, 3,425 measurements; of 18 wells with long records, 12 show the water table getting deeper since 1990; sanity passed
sources.notes: Depth below land surface: a larger number means a deeper water table. Readings flagged as taken during or just after pumping are excluded from trends. A well a few kilometres from a field describes the aquifer, not that field's own well.
